data.text: [00:00]CD2 Track 18
D = Deepa, F = Fiona
[00:04]Hi Fiona. What’s the matter?

[00:07]I don’t know. I’d like to meet someone nice … you know, a nice boyfriend. `[00:14]I feel that I’ve totally got over Daniel now. `[00:17.8]You know, we just grew apart really … and then we finally split up with each other at Thanksgiving. `[00:24]Ermm … well, it was in November. `[00:28]Oh, actually – I remember now, we split up on my birthday – on the eighteenth of November!
[00:35]Oh dear …

[00:36.6]I’m fine now, but … I haven’t found anyone nice to go out with since then, and I don’t know where to meet anyone. `[00:44.9]There’s nobody at work, that’s for sure! … How did you meet your husband?
[00:50.8]Oh, I was lucky, I suppose … . My parents helped me.
[00:54.9]Your parents? Really?

[00:57]Yes, it’s the Indian tradition; you know, arranged marriage. `[01:02]It’s different now, though. `[01:04]Nobody forces you to get married to someone you don’t like. `[01:07.7]Your parents help you find someone, but you can say ‘no’ if you don’t like him. `[01:12]You certainly don’t have to put up with someone you don’t like for the rest of your life!
[01:17]So, what did you do?

[01:19.9]Well, like a lot of young Asians from Britain, I went to India for a couple of months in the winter. `[01:26]The winter is ‘wedding season’ – lots of people get married at that time. `[01:31.9]Indian weddings last about a week, and they are a really good place to meet other young single people.
[01:38]Really?

[01:38.7]Yes, so my parents came with me and they arranged for me to go to lots of social events. `[01:45]I spent most of the time going to weddings and parties, and visiting lots of friends and family. `[01:51.8]I met loads of single men there and some of them took me out on dates.
[01:56.9]So, you meet people properly and talk to them in a social situation?
[02:01.9]Yes, it’s all very normal really. `[02:05]The thing that’s different is that it’s all speeded up. `[02:08.9]I mean, most parents would like everything done in about one or maybe two months.
[02:14.4]One or two months?

[02:15.8]Yes, I arrived in India in December … at the beginning of December … and I got married at the end of January – on the 28th of January actually. `[02:26]When I came back to Britain, I was a married woman!
[02:29.7]Really?! That is quick!
[02:32.7]Yes. The whole process is really fast – meeting people, going out with different boyfriends and then getting married. Job done!
[02:42]It’s a bit like speed-dating!
[02:44.8]Speed-dating? Have you ever done that?

[02:47.7]Yes, I did it once. `[02:49.8]It was OK, but you only have three minutes to talk to each person and it feels very unreal. `[02:57.8]It really is like a job interview and you don’t get enough time.
[03:02.5]Mmm … The arranged marriage thing is different because although it’s quick, you have time to get to know someone in a real social situation.
[03:11.8]Yes, with speed dating you meet twenty people in one hour! And I was there for two hours!
[03:19]Sounds quite fun though – did you meet anyone you liked?
[03:22.8]Well, there was one who was quite nice …
